decisions: K is the 0-based index of the log write (the K-th line the shim sees, counting a continuation write of a short write as part of its line): K lines are complete before it, so acked == K and, for a stop in write K, m == K; the prereg's formulas need this reading.

k (the cut of P1 and S) is drawn over the line WITHOUT its newline, 1..len(body)-1: with the prereg's literal 1..len(line)-1 the largest k would write a complete JSON object without its newline, which parses and is not a fragment. The heal newline, when present, is extra.

A planned stop that never happens (the shim never reached its point, e.g. a mutant that removes the fsync the P2/P3 stop waits on), a kill that is not preceded by WIFSTOPPED, a worker that exits non-zero or whose shim count is below its appends is INVALID (reported, never a pass).
The log file is created empty by the parent before the writers are spawned (the shim matches it by device and inode); the writers open it O_CREAT as usual.
'max survivor append wall while a holder was stopped' is the largest append wall of any survivor in the run (the run contains every holder stop); it is not split per stop.
E-interleave-t: the 0.2 s window starts after B has entered append (B signals first), so B's append wall is >= 0.2 s by construction when the lock holds; B's wall is measured in B.
E-interleave-p: B's go-to-done wall is measured by the parent; 'B done in the window' means its done line arrived within 0.2 s of the go line.
E-kill-import: K ~ U{1..25} is the 0-based write index, so K events are complete and the re-import writes 27-K events.
The control is built by 'git archive a4ab4a1 lattice' into <scratch>/control (not the shared clone of round 1); the tested arm's workers run with PYTHONPATH=this checkout.

post_hoc_script_corrections.when: after the first --mutants run (aborted at IK7; log kept as run-mutants-aborted.txt, no mutants.json written)
post_hoc_script_corrections.old: IK4 hunk new text 'os.pread(fd, 1, size)  # MUTANT IK4' and IK7 hunk new text 'fcntl.LOCK_SH | fcntl.LOCK_NB  # MUTANT IK7' (trailing comments in mid-expression)
post_hoc_script_corrections.new: no trailing comment in either hunk: the comment swallowed the rest of the line, so IK4 became 'torn = size > 0 and b""' (no heal at all: IK2's semantics, not the intended always-a-prefix) and IK7 did not compile; the aborted run's IK4 verdict is void. make_mutant also now runs inside the per-mutant try (an uncompilable mutant is reported as an error, not a crash)

post_hoc_script_corrections.when: smoke trial (--quick, scratch out) before any recorded run
post_hoc_script_corrections.old: Shim._stop printed the stop line with print(...) to sys.stdout
post_hoc_script_corrections.new: print(..., file=sys.__stdout__): an import-plan worker redirects sys.stdout while the CLI runs, so the stop line went into a StringIO and the parent never saw it (a stopped worker hung the trial; killed by hand)

post_hoc_script_corrections.when: control smoke trial before any recorded run

post_hoc_script_corrections.new: an event lacking them is counted as 'malformed_parseable' (a glued head with a foreign tail that still parses as JSON, a control-arm phenomenon) and excluded from the (w, t, seq) sets; the old code raised KeyError and reported the probe as ERROR
